conviction_note: Q3 itself looks in line: capacity +16.3% and load factor 88.6% are public, and my cost arithmetic (CASM-ex 5.7c, Q3 fuel near $3.9-4.0) lands on the roughly 16-18% margin consensus implies. The print turns on the FY26 guide (17-19% margin at $3.60/gal fuel), which peers' Q4 fuel assumptions ($4.25-4.85) make very likely to be cut. But a cut is widely expected: consensus EPS is down 4.5-8.8% in 30 days, the stock is down 9.6% in 5 sessions on an airline-wide oil selloff, and skew is mildly put-bid. So the findings net to about 0 and p_up sits at 48. abs_move 7.0 comes from the rebuilt reaction history (-10.5%, +7.9%, -5.8%) and the 5.56% implied move, with a guidance change likely.

positioning_check: Short interest is about 1.5M shares, 3.6% of float, 5.9 days to cover, settlement 2026-10-05 per Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/cpa/summary). That is not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. Baseline skew_25d is +2.12 vol points, mildly downside-paid; put/call OI is 0.94 on thin OI of 2,495 with a 30% ATM spread. The tape is down 9.63% over 5 sessions and 1.11% over 20, and sits 14.35% below the 52-week high. The 5-day drop coincides with an airline-wide selloff on rebounding oil (2026-11-12: Delta -5.2%, United -6.0%, all eight US carriers worth over $2bn down; https://www.trefis.com/stock/dal/articles/624912/why-did-delta-stock-fall/2026-11-13).

findings.finding: Copa's FY26 guide (17-19% operating margin) assumes $3.60/gal all-in fuel. With Q1 at $2.73 and Q2 at $4.28, that implies about $3.7 for H2. Every counterparty that has reported since points well above that for Q4: United guided Q4 fuel to about $4.80 against $3.90 in Q3; LATAM (Nov 3) moved its Q4 jet assumption to $180/bbl from $130 in August and cut its EBITDA guide; Volaris cut its FY EBITDAR margin; IATA's latest global average is $169.82/bbl (about $4.04/gal, down 5.1% w/w). Copa does not hedge, so a cut to the FY margin guide (my arithmetic: about 15-16%) and a higher fuel assumption are likely in the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (released 2026-08-05 after the close) cut the FY margin guide from 22-24% to 17-19% and missed EPS ($1.67 vs about $1.88). The stock went 150.78 to 142.05, -5.8% (Yahoo chart bars). Q3 2025 (released 2025-11-19 after the close) went 126.44 to 113.11, -10.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. If the market had fully priced a cut, we would expect what we see: consensus Q3 EPS cut 4.5-8.8% in 30 days (Chartmill, Zacks), the stock down 9.6% in 5 sessions with the airline group, and put-leaning skew. The residual is the size of the cut: a cut below 15%, or the Q4 bookings commentary, could still surprise. Sell-side FY estimates are not sourced here.
findings.independence: Peer documents, not Copa's: United Q4 fuel guide about $4.80 (https://finsee.ai/earnings/ual/2026/q3/en/, 2026-10-20); LATAM Q4 assumption $180/bbl vs $130 and EBITDA guide cut (https://www.airwaysmag.com/new-post/latam-q3-2026-results-fuel-costs-earnings-outlook, 2026-11-03); IATA fuel monitor $169.82/bbl (https://www.iata.org/en/publications/economics/fuel-monitor/). This is macro-to-company transmission: Copa has not spoken since 2026-08-05.

findings.finding: Q3 operating data in Copa's own 6-Ks: ASMs 9,576.8M (Jul 3,316.7 + Aug 3,219.1 + Sep 3,041.0), +16.3% y/y against 8,238.1M, above the FY ASM guide of 14-15%. Load factor was 88.6% against 88.0%. Consensus revenue of $1.185B implies RASM of about 12.37c, +11.7% y/y against 11.08c ($913.1M / 8,238.1M). Management's H2 RASM outlook was about +10%, which would mean about $1.167B. On cost, CASM-ex 5.7c plus about 107M gallons at $3.9-4.0 gives an operating margin of about 17-18%, against about 16% implied by the $3.87 EPS consensus. Q3 looks in line to slightly better on margin, with revenue at or slightly under consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat on EPS and revenue (Zacks headline) and the stock rose about +7.9% (2026-05-05 close 113.61 to 2026-05-06 close 122.55; release date assumed 2026-05-05 after the close, not confirmed). Q3 2025 beat on EPS but missed revenue (Zacks headline) and fell -10.5%. Reported-quarter beats have not reliably been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: The traffic is fully public. The cost and fuel arithmetic is mine and points to an in-line quarter, which is what consensus already holds. It lands inside what the company guided, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Q3 counterparty unit revenue was strong in the region. United's Latin America unit revenue rose 31% on 5% less capacity (https://finsee.ai/earnings/ual/2026/q3/en/). LATAM's passenger unit revenue rose 9.4% (https://www.airwaysmag.com/new-post/latam-q3-2026-results-fuel-costs-earnings-outlook). Volaris reported double-digit TRASM, with US Gulf Coast jet at $3.67/gal in Q3 (https://finviz.com/news/408220/volaris-reports-financial-results-for-the-third-quarter-2026-1-billion-revenue-up-32-yoy). The July and August data come from separate 6-Ks: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1345105/000162828026052826/cpa-20260804xexx991.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1345105/000162828026061420/cpa-20260909xexx991.htm.

findings.finding: October 2026 ASM growth slowed to +11.5% (3,125.3M) from +15.7% in September and +16.2-16.8% in July-August, with load factor 87.4% (+0.2pt). Copa appears to be trimming Q4 capacity growth into the fuel spike. That supports Q4 RASM, since United's +31% Latin unit revenue came on cut capacity, and it suggests the FY ASM guide of 14-15% may be trimmed, a yield-positive way to defend the margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved instance of a Copa capacity-guide trim found. The FY capacity guide was raised at Q2 (to 14-15% from 11-13%), alongside the margin cut that sold -5.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The October release came out on Nov 12, the same day as the airline-wide oil selloff, and wire copy headlined only load factor (CAPA: 'load factor at 87%'). If the market were reading it as capacity discipline, CPA would have held up better than US carriers that week; instead it fell with them, -9.6% over 5 sessions. The causal reading (deliberate trim versus calendar or fleet timing) is my inference and is unconfirmed.
findings.independence: United's Q3 pattern, unit revenue up most where it cut flying (https://finsee.ai/earnings/ual/2026/q3/en/), and LATAM trimming its FY capacity guide to 8.5-9.5% from 9-10% (https://www.airwaysmag.com/new-post/latam-q3-2026-results-fuel-costs-earnings-outlook) point the same way for the industry. Neither is Copa.

findings.finding: Copa is expanding Venezuela, a historically high-yield market, in Q4 2026: a third daily Panama-Caracas flight from 2026-11-01 and Margarita Island (6th Venezuelan destination) from 2026-11-26. This is a small Q4 yield tailwind the outlook may cite.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public network news, mostly priced, and small relative to a system growing 11-16%. It is filed because the sweep flagged Venezuela.
findings.independence: Margarita launch reported separately by Aviacionaldia (https://aviacionaldia.com/en/2026/08/margarita-island-becomes-copa-airlines-sixth-venezuelan-destination.html, 2026-08).

findings.finding: Into the print, CPA fell 9.63% over 5 sessions (Nov 13 close $140.87, $134.63 at the seal) in an airline-wide oil-driven selloff (2026-11-12: Delta -5.2%, United -6.0%, all eight US carriers worth over $2bn down). Since then IATA's global jet fuel average fell 5.1% w/w to $169.82/bbl, against $190.18 for the week of Oct 9. Short interest is only 3.6% of float. Some of the expected guide cut is therefore already in the tape, and fuel has eased from its October peak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 came after the March fuel-spike drawdown and rose +7.9%. Q2 2026 came after a run to $150.78 and fell -5.8%. The reaction has tracked what was priced going in.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning, not information. If the drawdown were Copa-specific bad news, it would show up in Copa's own documents or wire stories, and none were found; it matches sector beta to oil. That is a weak relief mechanism, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: IATA fuel monitor (https://www.iata.org/en/publications/economics/fuel-monitor/, undated latest week) and the Oct 9 IATA figure of $190.18/bbl (https://www.gulf-times.com/article/731943/business/middle-east-maintains-lowest-global-jet-fuel-price-despite-80-annual-rise-iata). The same fuel data underlies the guidance finding: one fact, read in opposite directions on two lines (FY guide level vs. what is already priced).

baseline_tension: The main negative (a likely FY guide cut on fuel) agrees with the mild put skew and the 9.6% five-day drop, so it is largely priced. The small positives (Q4 capacity trim, fuel off its October peak, a light short base) cut slightly against the skew, so the net is near zero and p_up sits just below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (a finding inside what the company guided is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect): the Q3 in-line finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 2 (guidance is the line that moves the stock; Q2 2026's guide cut sold -5.8%) weighed against the skew-agreement discount: the guidance finding stays at -1.5, unchanged.

Lesson on FPI reaction histories: the base rate was already rebuilt from confirmed release dates (Q3'25 -10.5%, Q1'26 +7.9%, Q2'26 -5.8%) rather than the empty baseline history; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged.
